- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak or negative, especially if recent price action is volatile; adjust upward by 1–3% if sentiment < 0.33 for 3+ days.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits mean reversion bias — if recent 10-day average is >72.5, model tends to overpredict; if <70.5, underpredict; use 71.5 as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (no sentiment), model tends to ignore trend; force a slight upward bias if price is trending down, or downward if trending up.
